Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.controlcenter

Class ControlPanelRegistry

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.controlcenter.ControlPanelRegistry
public final class ControlPanelRegistry extends Object
Discovers the control center's category panels. The built-in panels (Appearance, Customization, Desktop, Display, Sound, Power, Mouse invalid input: '&' Keyboard, Shortcuts, Notifications, Workspaces, Quick Launch, Default Applications, Network, Bluetooth, Printing, Date invalid input: '&' Time, Language invalid input: '&' Region, Users, System, Services, System Update, Storage, Schedule, Task Scheduler) are registered on first access; extra panels can be contributed with register(ControlPanel) before the control center window is built.

Categories are registered as ControlPanelRegistry.PanelDescriptors: the control center learns each category's name up front but the (potentially expensive) panel is constructed lazily, only when the user actually opens that category. This matters because building a panel can block on platform I/O - Network, Bluetooth, Printing, Date invalid input: '&' Time, Language invalid input: '&' Region and Mouse invalid input: '&' Keyboard shell out to nmcli / bluetoothctl / rfkill / lpstat / timedatectl / localectl / xset, Appearance scans the wallpaper directory and decodes thumbnails, System reads /proc - so constructing all of them eagerly froze the window for seconds before it even appeared. A panel that cannot be constructed in this JVM (a missing Java 3D runtime, say) yields null from ControlPanelRegistry.PanelDescriptor.get() rather than throwing, so one bad category cannot take the whole control center with it.

Every panel registers in each desktop mode, so the control center shows the same categories on the 3D desktop and on the conventional Swing (2D) desktop. The Appearance and Desktop panels drive whichever desktop is running: on the 3D desktop they post events through lg3d's connector (wallpaper textures, taskbar re-layout), and on the 2D desktop they call into Desktop2D instead, so the same settings take live effect there.

  • Method Details

    • register

      public static void register(ControlPanel panel)
      Registers an additional, already-constructed category panel. Skipped if a category with the same display name is already registered.

    • descriptors

      public static List<ControlPanelRegistry.PanelDescriptor> descriptors()
      The registered category descriptors, in display order (defaults included). Listing them constructs nothing, so the control center can show its navigation immediately and build each panel on demand.

    • panels

      public static List<ControlPanel> panels()
      The registered panels, in display order, constructing any not yet built. Retained for callers that genuinely want every panel up front; the control center shell itself uses descriptors() and builds lazily. Panels that cannot be constructed are omitted.
